title: Onboarding Zscaler Hosted Azure Tenant or Management Group

blocks.text: You can onboard an Azure tenant or management group and their associated subscriptions. AI Security monitors and scans the data stores (e.g., virtual machines, storage accounts) in the onboarded subscriptions to identify sensitive data, misconfigurations, and vulnerabilities.
Before onboarding an Azure tenant or management group, ensure you have completed the following:

blocks.item: Create the following in the Microsoft Entra ID:
Azure application or service principal: To provide AI Security access to the resources within the target subscriptions. To learn more, refer to the Microsoft documentation.
See instructions.
Sign in to the Azure portal and go to Microsoft Entra ID.
In the left-side navigation, go to Manage > App registrations.
The App registrations page appears.
On the App registrations page, click + New registration.
The Register an application page appears.
On the Register an application page, provide the following details and click Register.
Name: Enter a unique name for the application.
Supported account types: Select the subscription.
The application is created in the Entra ID. Copy the Application (client) ID and save them on your system as this is required while onboarding.
See image.
Client secret: If you want to create an integration using client secret which is a confidential string that is used as a password for the application created.
See instructions.
Sign in to the Azure portal and go to Microsoft Entra ID.
In the left-side navigation, go to Manage > App registrations.
The App registrations page appears.
On the App registrations page, search for and select the application you created.
In the left-side navigation, go to Manage > Certificates & Secrets.
On the Client secrets tab, click + New client secret.
See image.
The Add a client secret drawer appears.
In the Add a client secret drawer:
Description: Enter a description for the client secret.
Expires: Select the expiration date from the drop-down menu.
Click Add.
In the Client secrets table, under Value, click the Copy icon to copy the string to the clipboard.
See image.
API permissions: Add API permissions and grant admin consent to the application to access resources within the subscription.
See instructions.
Sign in to the Azure portal and go to Microsoft Entra ID.
In the left-side navigation, go to Manage > App registrations.
The App registrations page appears.
On the App registrations page, search for and select the application you created.
In the left-side navigation, go to Manage > API permissions.
Click + Add a permissions.
The Request API permissions drawer appears.
On the Request API permissions drawer, select Microsoft Graph and add the following permissions:
See image.

table: Sign in and read user profile
Read all policies for privileged role assignments of your company's directory

blocks.item: Entitlements are affected if the optional API permissions are not configured.
On the API permissions page, click Grant admin consent for <application name>.
In the Grand admin consent confirmation window, click Yes.
Ensure you have the following roles to deploy the templates and grant API permissions.

table: Root Tenant Management Group Target Subscription
User Access Administrator (Based on your onboarding scope)
Storage Account Contributor (For Terraform State File)
Privileged Role Administrator (For granting the API permission)

blocks.item: Install the latest versions
of Terraform and Azure CLIs to run the templates. To learn more, refer to the Microsoft documentation.

Identify the storage containers where Terraform state files must be stored. The state files are required to manage resources created by the AI Security Terraform templates and to upgrade to new templates. You can also create the following new storage containers to store the state files:
Resource Group
Resource groups are logical containers that comprises a group of Azure resources. To learn more, refer to the Microsoft documentation.
To create a resource group:
Sign in to the Azure portal and go to Resource groups.
Click +Create.
See image.
The Create a resource group drawer appears
In the Create a resource group drawer, on the Basics tab:
Subscription: Select the orchestrator subscription from the drop-down menu.
Resource group: Enter a unique name for the resource group.
Region: Select a region where the resource group must be created.
Click Review + create.
See image.
Storage Account
Storage accounts store data objects such as files, queues, tables, and Terraform state files. To learn more, refer to the Microsoft documentation.
To create a storage account:
Sign in to the Azure portal and go to Storage account.
Click +Create.
See image.
The Create a storage account drawer appears.
In the Create a storage account window, on the Basics tab:
Subscription: Select your Azure subscription.
Resource group: Select the resource group that you created.
Storage account name: Enter a unique name for the storage account.
Region: Select location where the storage account must be created.
Click Review + create.
See image.
Storage Account Container
A storage account container is a set of blobs similar to a directory in a file system. To learn more, refer to the Microsoft documentation.
To create a storage account container:
Sign in to the Azure portal and go to Storage account.
Locate the storage account you created and click the storage account.
In the left-side navigation, under Data storage, select Containers.
See image.
Click +Container.
See image.
In the New container drawer:
Name: Enter a unique name for the container.
Anonymous access level: Select the access level for the container.
See image.
Click Create.

blocks.heading: Onboarding an Azure Tenant or Management Group

blocks.text: To onboard an Azure tenant or management group:

blocks.item: 1. Select a Deployment Mode.
To onboard an Azure tenant or management group, you must first select the deployment mode.
In the Zscaler Admin Console, go to Administration > Account Onboarding.
Click Add New.
In the Select Cloud Provider window, for Select Cloud Type, click the Azure tile.
See image.
Click Next.
In the Select Deployment Mode window, choose Zscaler Hosted.
See image.
Click Next.
2. Select an Onboarding Scope.
In the Select Onboarding Scope section, select one of the following and click Next.
Tenant: To onboard the entire Azure AD tenant. A role assignment is created at the tenant root management group, enabling discovery of every subscription in the tenant.
Management Group: To onboard subscriptions under a specific management group and its descendants. This is the recommended approach when Zscaler coverage is needed for only part of the tenant.
Subscription: To onboard a single Azure subscription without requiring tenant enumeration.
See image.
3. Select a Configuration Creation Mode.
In the Configuration Creation Mode section, select one of the following and click Next.
Automated Role Creation: To allow Zscaler to generate Terraform modules for the custom role and role assignment using the azurerm provider.
See image.
Manual Role Creation: To create a custom role and assign roles using the existing workflow.
4. Complete Tenant Discovery.
In the Tenant Discovery section, provide the following Azure AD tenant details so Zscaler can enumerate management groups and subscriptions in scope and click Next.
Azure Tenant Details:
Integration Alias: Enter a user-friendly name for the subscription.
Tenant ID: Enter the Microsoft Entra tenant ID. You can find the tenant ID in the Azure portal in multiple ways. For example:
Sign in to the Azure portal.
On the top right, select your account and then click Switch directory.
On the Portal Settings | Directories + subscriptions page, under All Directories, copy the Directory ID of the corresponding tenant that you want to onboard.
Zscaler App (Client) ID: Enter the application or client ID.

Management Group ID: Enter the Management Group ID. This field appears if you have selected Management Group as an option in the Select Onboarding Scope section. You can find the management group ID under Resource Manager > Organization > Management groups in Azure Portal.
See image.

Notification Emails (Optional): Enter the email addresses of the recipients who must be notified of any configuration or permissions issues encountered with the onboarded tenant. You can add up to 30 email addresses to receive notifications about the issues. You can also add email addresses after completing the onboarding process.
App Registration Credentials: This is required for Zscaler to authenticate your Azure AD app registration before the tenant enumeration begins. Select from one of the following
Client Secret
To use client secret as authentication for app registration, do the following:
Client Secret: Enter the client secret generated as a pre-requisite in the Azure portal.
Save Integration: To register the integration in the Zscaler backend. Subsequent onboarding steps reference the returned integration ID.
See image.
Certificate
Zscaler Generate the client certificate to use a certificate-based authentication for app registration. To generate a client certificate, do the following:
Save Integration: To register the integration in the Zscaler backend. Subsequent onboarding steps reference the returned integration ID.

Download and Validate the Certificate: Download the client certificate generated by Zscaler for this integration. Upload it to your Azure AD app registration under Certificates & secrets > Certificates.
See image.
Grant Reader Role to Zscaler: Copy the PowerShell one-liner and run it in the Azure Portal to assign the built-in Reader role to the Zscaler service principal at the tenant root scope.
See image.

Discovery in the next step fails if this step is not completed. Ensure the Az PowerShell module is installed, and you are signed in with Connect-AzAccount as a User Access Administrator or Owner on the target scope. The Zscaler app must also have admin consent granted in your Azure AD.
Discover Tenant Hierarchy: Click Discover to enumerate the management groups and subscriptions that Zscaler has read access to. If discovery fails, click Re-Discover.
5. Define Scope Selection.

In the Scope selection section, select the management groups and subscriptions to include in the scan. Enable autodetection on any management group where all current subscriptions are selected to automatically onboard future subscriptions.
See image.

Custom role definitions are created at the tenant root level and propagate to the selected subscriptions. You can add or remove subscriptions from the integration's Accounts tab with re-onboarding required.
6. Configure Business Unit Mapping.
In the Business Unit Mapping section, you can do the following and click Next.
Select a subscription to map a subscription to a business unit for filtering and reporting inside Zscaler.
Click + New Business Unit to add a new business unit.
All subscriptions are assigned to a business unit. If no mapping is specified, then the Default option is applied.
See image.
7. Select Services.

In the Service Selection section, select the scanning services you want to enable for this integration. Each service you enable adds a specific, scoped set of Azure permissions to the Scanning custom role, ensuring that only the permissions required for the selected services are granted.
See image.
8. Provide Configuration Details.
In the Configuration section, provide the following details and click Next.
Integration and Identity:
Integration Alias: User name set at the time of tenant discovery is autopopulated.
Application (Client ID): The application or client ID set at the time of tenant discovery is autopopulated.
Custom Roles
If you choose automated role creation: The following role names are used for the Azure custom role by the Terraform modules:
Asset Discovery Role Name
Scanning Role Name
See image.

If you choose manual role creation: Assign a custom role definition with the required Azure permissions to the Zscaler service principal at your target scope. Use the Application (Client) ID name as the principalld. Ensure your custom role is defined at the Management Group or Tenant scope depending on your onboarding scope. The role assignment is performed at the Subscription scope.
See image.

Evidence Storage (Optional): AI Security discovers files and tables containing sensitive data and generates snippets of evidence data to investigate and validate the findings. You can choose an existing storage account container or add a new one to store these evidence snippets.
Evidence Role Name: The name of the evidence role.
Storage Account Resource ID: The resource ID of the storage account.
Container Name: The name of the container.

In case of manual role creation: Assign a custom role definition with the required Azure permissions to the Zscaler service principal at your target scope so it can write evidence collected during scans. Use the Application (Client) ID above as the principalId. Ensure your custom role is defined at the Storage account Subscription scope and the role assignment is performed at the evidence Storage accoun
See image.
Tags (Optional): Configure custom tags to identify the resources created by AI Security.
Click Add Tag, and enter key-value pairs to add more tags.
9. Review & Deploy.
In the Review & Deploy section, do the following:

If you have selected Automated Role Creation option: Download and deploy the Terraform modules in your Azure environment and then validate that Zscaler can access the scoped APIs before completing onboarding.
See image.
After deploying the Terraform module against the target scope, click Save & Complete Onboarding.
If you have selected the Manual Role Creation option: Zscaler authenticates using the Application (Client) ID and validates that each custom role assignment grants the required permissions.
See image.
After creating the custom roles and assigning them at the target scope, click Save & Complete Onboarding.
